rounds.text: The business operates within the Capital Goods sector, which currently enjoys a supportive macro backdrop with a tailwind score of +1.04 [E65, E66], alongside sector median profit and sales growth of 22.1% and 18.6% respectively [E67, E68]. Demonstrating strong long-term profit compounding, the company has grown profits at 23% over 10 years, 42% over 5 years, and 34% over 3 years, complemented by a 49% profit growth in the trailing twelve months [E14, E15, E16, E17]. Furthermore, the company maintains a conservative financial profile, having actively reduced its debt to Rs 1.76 Cr in March 2026 down from Rs 2.94 Cr previously, resulting in a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.19x [E30, E31, E47]. Operational efficiency has also seen notable improvement, highlighted by debtor days narrowing dramatically from 220 down to 33.0 days [E49], and a solid 3-year median ROE track record of nearly 30% [E48]. Market strength is clearly evident through a maximum relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500, a share price positioned above its 200-day moving average, and a 3-year compounded share price growth of 134% [E18, E38, E39]. Conceded: the company faces significant near-term headwinds including a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of -98%, a negative operating cash flow of Rs -0.17 Cr for March 2026, and a rich price-to-book ratio of 16.17x [E1, E13, E27].

The valuation and fundamentals of IKOMA Technologies Limited are heavily disconnected, highlighted by a staggering price-to-book ratio of 16.17x against a book value of ₹ 3.97 [E1], which is drastically higher than the sector benchmark P/B of 2.61x [E6]. Operational performance has sharply deteriorated, evidenced by a catastrophic compounded sales growth of -98% over the trailing twelve months [E13] and an operating margin collapse to -614% in the TTM from 19% three years earlier [E22]. Cash generation is deeply problematic, with operating cash flow and free cash flow both plunging to negative Rs -0.17 Cr in March 2026 alongside a negative cash conversion of -0.74x [E26, E28]. Furthermore, return metrics are severely depressed, with an ROE of just 2.5% [E12] and ROCE at 3.1% [E11], both vastly trailing sector benchmarks [E8, E9]. Promoter commitment is also waning as holdings have decreased to 37.72% in June 2026 from 41.87% in September 2023 [E33]. Conceded: the company boasts a strong relative-strength rating of 100 [E39], is positioned comfortably above its 200-day moving average [E38], and operates within a Capital Goods sector tailwind with a score of +1.04 [E66].

Conceded: P/B is 16.17x [E1], operating cash flow and free cash flow were negative at Rs -0.17 Cr [E27, E28], and TTM compounded sales growth reads -98% [E13]. However, the bear ignores powerful structural strengths and recent operational improvements that prove the stock is under-appreciated. The business is conservatively financed with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.19x [E30], having successfully reduced its total borrowings from Rs 2.94 Cr to Rs 1.76 Cr [E31] alongside explicit flags for debt reduction [E47]. Working capital management has seen a remarkable transformation, with debtor days compressing dramatically from 220 down to 33.0 days [E49]. Profitability displays powerful multi-year and recent compounding, boasting a 10-year profit growth of 23% [E14], 5-year profit growth of 42% [E15], 3-year profit growth of 34% [E16], and a strong 49% profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E17]. Furthermore, the company maintains an exceptional historical return profile with a 3-year median ROE of 30% [E20] and a multi-year track record recognized at nearly 30% [E48], outperforming the broader market with a perfect relative-strength rating of 100 [E39] while riding a strong Capital Goods sector tailwind score of +1.04 [E66].

Conceded: borrowings are down to Rs 1.76 Cr [E31], debtor days have improved to 33.0 days [E49], and multi-year profit compounding exists [E14, E15, E16, E17]. However, the bull's reliance on past profit growth ignores the catastrophic collapse happening right now, evidenced by a TTM compounded sales growth of -98% [E13], a net profit drop of -97% YoY [E60], and a sales plunge of -92% YoY [E61]. The claim of a conservative financial structure is undermined by a low interest coverage ratio [E52], while the touted historical ROE of 30% [E20] has collapsed to a meager 3% over the last year [E21, E63]. Operating and free cash flows are negative at Rs -0.17 Cr [E27, E28], cash conversion sits at an alarming -0.74x [E26], and operating margins have crashed by 634 percentage points in the TTM to -614% [E22]. Furthermore, promoter commitment is demonstrably eroding, with holdings falling from 41.87% to 37.72% over time [E33] and declining by 16.9% over the last three years [E54]. Finally, paying a rich 16.17x price-to-book ratio [E1] for a business with a severe -92.5% historical peak-to-trough drawdown [E41] and decelerating earnings [E62] exposes shareholders to massive valuation risk despite sector tailwinds [E66].
